phrases.en: This is the call to Fajr prayer
phrases.notes: أَذَان = call to prayer. الْفَجْر = dawn, and also the name of the first prayer of the day.

phrases.en: Allah is greatest. Allah is greatest
phrases.notes: The words that open the adhan. أَكْبَر = greater/greatest. Said twice in a row.
Same أَيْنَ as in Dialogue 2. الْأَوْلَاد = the children (plural of وَلَد, seen in Dialogue 3).

phrases.en: Sa'd is in the bathroom making wudu
phrases.notes: فِي = in. الْحَمَّام = the bathroom. يَتَوَضَّأ = he makes wudu — the ablution before prayer.
Same أَيْنَ question as before, with وَ in front — 'and where is …?'.

phrases.en: Sa'id is in the room reading the Qur'an
phrases.notes: الْغُرْفَة = the room. يَقْرَأ = he reads. الْقُرْآن = the Qur'an. Same shape as the previous line — فِي … يَ…ُ.
Same question a third time. The father is working through all the children in turn.

phrases.en: Sa'idah is in the prayer room praying
phrases.notes: الْمُصَلَّى = the prayer room. تُصَلِّي = she prays — the feminine form, matching سَعِيدَة.
No وَ this time — this isn't a continuation of the previous question but a fresh one. الْمُصْطَفَى = 'the chosen one', here used as a name.

phrases.en: This is al-Mustafa, O my father
phrases.notes: يَا = O — used before a name or title when addressing someone. وَالِدِي = my father, the same word seen in Dialogue 1 (Family Photo).
النَّظَّارَة = the glasses. The same 'and where is …?' question, but this is the first time it doesn't refer to a person.

phrases.en: This is the glasses, O my father
phrases.notes: Same shape as line 10, but feminine: هَذِهِ هِيَ instead of هَذَا هُوَ — because النَّظَّارَة is feminine.
هَيَّا بِنَا = 'let's go' / 'come on'. إِلَى = to. الْمَسْجِد = the mosque.
The same phrase the father just said — the sons answer him by repeating it.
